meta.first_line: yabe rūpa-sanātana vraje gelā dui jana

title: Śrīla Raghunāth Dās Goswāmī Śochaka
author: unknown composer, from the Maṭh’s Śrī Gauḍīya Gitāñjali
subtitle: Śrīla Raghunāth Dās’ Deep Sorrow
Kīrtan One

text: yabe rūpa-sanātana    vraje gelā dui jana
translation: When Raghunāth Dās heard that Rūpa and Sanātan went to Vraja, he gave up the proprietorship of his estate and he gave up pleasures equal to those of Indra, and came to the Lord’s side.

text: uṭhi’ rātre niśā-bhāge    duyāre praharī jāge
kṣudhā tṛṣṇā nāhi pāya    manodvege chali’ yāya
translation: He arose in the dark very early in the morning, avoided the main road, and travelled on an alternate path. He felt no hunger or thirst as he ran anxiously. He thought constantly of Śrī Chaitanya’s feet.

text: eka gopa dugdha dilā    tāhā kheye viśrāmilā
translation: One day in a village in the evening he sat in a cowshed chanting, “O Chaitanya!” and a cowherd boy gave him some milk. He drank it, rested, and remained there for the night.

text: ye aṅga pālaṅka vine    bhūmi-śayyā nāhi jāne
translation: His body had never experienced lying on the ground without a bed­stead, but his feet now walked over thorns.

text: yi̐ho belā daṇḍa chāri    tolā jale snāna kari’
ebe yadi kichhu pāna    sandhyā-kāle tāhā khāna
translation: He used to bathe with raised water at mid-morning and eat meals comprised of the six tastes, but now he would eat in the evening if he found something, and would lie down without eating anything if he did not.

text: bāra dinera patha yāna    tina sandhyā anna khāna
dekhiyā se śrī-mandira    du-nayane vahe nīra
translation: After travelling the path for twelve days and eating solid food on only three of these days in the evening, he entered the city of Nīlāchal. Seeing the Temple, tears poured from his eyes, and he called out, “O Chaitanya!”
This Rādhā Vallabha Dās longs, “Where is my Raghunāth Dās? Just by his association, the hair on my body stands on end. I pray for the dust of his feet.”
